message.content: {"items": [{"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "The combined model achieves the lowest RMSE (0.003365) among all passing structures, indicating that sensor bias, velocity offset, and speed step together best explain the observed position deviations.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(VELOCITY_OFFSET,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "This two-factor model has a very low RMSE (0.003401), nearly matching the three-factor model, suggesting velocity offset and speed step are the primary drivers of the discrepancy.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,SPEED_STEP)", "rationale": "This model also performs well with an RMSE of 0.003811, indicating that sensor bias combined with speed step is a strong explanatory structure.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "SPEED_STEP", "rationale": "As a single-factor model, SPEED_STEP achieves the lowest RMSE (0.00527), suggesting a change in belt speed is a significant contributor to the observed errors.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "SENSOR_BIAS", "rationale": "The SENSOR_BIAS model has a low RMSE (0.006362) and is supported by the context noting the position sensor was recently calibrated but stability should be checked.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "VELOCITY_OFFSET", "rationale": "The VELOCITY_OFFSET model has a comparable RMSE (0.006607) to SENSOR_BIAS, indicating a constant velocity offset is also a plausible explanation for the position drift.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}, {"hypothesis_id": "AND(SENSOR_BIAS,VELOCITY_OFFSET)", "rationale": "Combining sensor bias and velocity offset yields an RMSE of 0.006229, which is slightly better than either factor alone, suggesting both may be present.", "evidence_refs": ["obs:0:1.200"]}]}
